content.text:
I submitted **index 137** (Cr 0.37, Fe 0.21, V 0.42). It had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, at 3.8×10⁻⁷ A.

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.10 / 0.41 / 0.49 | 7×10⁻⁸ A |
| 15 | 0.25 / 0.30 / 0.45 | 2×10⁻⁷ A |
| 137 | 0.37 / 0.21 / 0.42 | 3.8×10⁻⁷ A |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose steadily as Cr went up and Fe went down, with V held at about 0.42–0.49. I used my last merit measurement to follow that trend toward more Cr, and it paid off.
- **XRD:** indices 0, 15 and 9 all show the same main crystal phase, so the gain seems to come from composition within that phase rather than from a new phase. Index 9, which is richer in V, also shows a small extra peak that looks like a second phase (probably V₂O₅). I didn't measure its photocurrent.

The trend hadn't levelled off when the merit budget ran out, so the true best may have even more Cr. Index 149 (Cr 0.43) is the obvious next one to measure. I used 3 of the 5 XRD scans; the other 2 are unspent.
